TO QUASH THE CHARGE SHEET SUBMITTED BY THE 1st RESPONDENT IN C.C.NO.9494/2019 AGAINST THE PETITIONER 1 TO 3 BEFORE THE HONBLE ACJM, BANGALORE RURAL DISTRICT AS ANNEXURE-A.

AND QUASH THE FIR IN CR.NO.96/2018 FILED BY THE 1st RESPONDENT BEFORE THE ACJM, BANGALORE RURAL DISTRICT AS ANNEXURE - B AGAINST THE PETITIONER NO.1 TO 3 AND ETC.,
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner Nos.2 and 3 have challenged the prosecution launched against them in C.C.No.9494/2019 pending trial before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru Rural District (henceforth referred to as 'Trial Court') NC: 2023:KHC:46086 for the offences punishable under Sections 506, 420, 468, 447, 504, 471 read with Section 34 of IPC.
2.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru Rural District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
On the basis of the information furnished by respondent No.2 on 08.03.2018, a case in Crime No.96/2018 was registered by respondent No.1 for the offences punishable under Sections 468, 471,
420, 447, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.

The respondent No.2 alleged that her husband had purchased the vacant land in Sy.No.18/1A situate at Whitefield, K.R. Puram Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluk from M/s Siddivinayaka Builders and Developers in terms of a sale deed dated 15.02.2006.

She claimed that Mr. K.P. Bharathan, the erstwhile owner of the land bearing Sy.No.18/1A had sold it to M/s Siddivinayaka Builders and Developers, who got it converted for non-agricultural Mr Rajanna vs State Of Karnataka on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127192592/
2 residential use, which was later changed for commercial purpose.

She claimed that Mr. K.P.
Bharathan died in the year 2008.

She alleged that accused No.1 filed a suit in O.S.No.1321/2014 before the City Civil Court, Bangalore, for perpetual injunction in respect of the land bearing Sy.No.18/1A on the strength of a General Power of Attorney dated 18.08.1999 allegedly executed by Mr. K.P. Bharathan.
She alleged that accused Nos.1 and 2 on NC: 2023:KHC:46086 12.02.2018 barged into the property and threatened her of her life.

She claimed that the power of attorney set up by accused Nos.1 and 2 was forged and fraudulent which was evident from the very fact that the sale deed executed by accused No.1 in favour of accused No.2 was for a sum of Rs.35,00,000/-,
while the husband of respondent No.2 had purchased the property in the year 2005-06 at a sum of Rs.1,25,00,000/-.
3. Respondent No.1 took up investigation and filed a charge-sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 419, 420, 447, 465, 468, 471, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.

The Trial Court in terms of a cryptic order, took cognizance for the offences punishable under Sections 506, 420, 468,
447, 504, 471 read with Section 34 of IPC and registered C.C.No.9494/2019 and issued process to the accused.
4. Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioners are before this Court.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioners filed a memo on 07.03.2022 withdrawing the petition as against petitioner No.1.
Therefore, this petition is restricted only in so far as NC: 2023:KHC:46086 petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are concerned, who were arraigned as accused Nos.2 and 4 before the Trial Court.

6. The learned counsel for the petitioners contended that respondent No.2 and her children have now filed a suit in O.S.No.1290/2020 before the City Civil Judge, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru, for declaration that they are the owner of the property and for cancellation of the sale deed brought about by accused No.1 in favour of accused No.2.

entities.text: City Civil Judge, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
He submits that the Trial Court did not apply its mind before taking cognizance as there was no material to justify the offence under Sections 465,
468, 471 of IPC.

He contends that since the land in question is a vacant piece of land and as accused No.2 also has a sale deed in his name, an offence under Section 447 of IPC is not made out so far as accused No.2 is concerned.

He contends that the offence, if any, is made out against accused No.1,
who allegedly threatened respondent No.2 of her life.

Further more, he contends that accused No.4 was a witness to the General Power of Attorney executed by Mr. K.P. Bharathan in favour of accused No.1 and no criminality could be attributed to accused No.4.
He therefore, prays that the prosecution launched against the petitioners be set at naught.

Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the very fact that accused No.1 had conveyed the property to accused No.2 on the basis of the fraudulent power of attorney for consideration of Rs.35,00,000/- which too, was allegedly paid by cash in the year 2017, makes it doubtful as the husband of respondent no.2 had purchased the property in the year 2005-06 at a sum of Rs.1,25,00,000/-.

Further, he contends that Mr. K.P. Bharathan died in the year 2008 and Mr Rajanna vs State Of Karnataka on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127192592/
3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: therefore, accused No.1 could not have conveyed the property to accused No.2 in the year 2017.

8. The learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 on the other hand submitted that a charge- sheet is now filed and the Trial Court has taken cognizance of the offences mentioned above and therefore, this Court may not exercise jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to set at naught the prosecution.

9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1.
The charge-sheet is filed for the offences mentioned above.

The basis for the charge-sheet for the offence punishable under Sections 465, 468, 471 of IPC is that accused No.1 had forged a power of attorney of Mr. K.P. Bharathan and thereafter, executed the sale deed in favour of accused No.2 as the power of attorney of Mr. K.P. Bharathan.
However, a perusal of the charge-sheet discloses that the power of attorney was not seized by respondent No.1.

There was no comparison of the signatures of Mr. K.P. Bharathan found on the incriminating power of attorney with the sale deed executed by Mr. K.P. Bharathan in favour of M/s Siddivinayaka Builders and Developers.

Therefore, unless it is made out that a false document as defined under Section 464 of IPC is made out, an offence under Sections 465, 468, 471 of IPC cannot be held to have been committed by the petitioners.

In so far as offence punishable under Sections 419, 420 of IPC, it is not the case of respondent No.2 that the property in question was entrusted by Mr. K.P. Bharathan to accused No.1 and that he misusing the trust reposed by Mr. K.P. Bharathan had conveyed the property to accused No.2.

Therefore, it is difficult to accept that an offence under Sections 419, 420 of IPC was committed by the NC:
2023:KHC:46086 petitioners.
The Trial Court without looking into these material facts blindly took cognizance by a cryptic order.
Under the circumstances, the order taking cognizance deserves to be interfered with.
11. Consequently, this petition is allowed in part.

The order dated 20.08.2019 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru, taking cognizance of the offences punishable under Sections 506, 420, 468, 447, 504, 471 read with Section 34 of IPC is quashed.

The case is remitted to the Trial Court, which shall consider whether further investigation is required in the case to verify whether power of attorney set up by accused No.1 is in fact executed by Mr. K.P. Bharathan or not.
The Trial Court is directed to consider materials on record and thereafter, proceed in accordance with law.
